classification.difficultyReason: Find missing angles, establish vertex correspondence and select SSS or AAS; crucially, reject the pair whose equal numerical sides occupy different corresponding positions.

content.prompt: In each part below, say whether the two triangles are congruent. If they are congruent, write a congruence statement, including the appropriate congruence test.

spec.description: Horizontal pair of unshaded triangles with all six side measurements and vertex labels; no right-angle marks. Ordinary source blue lines become black.
spec.mathematics: AC=PR=10 cm; AB=PQ=20 cm; BC=QR=25 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied measurements remain visible; no congruence statement is supplied.

answer.worked: $AB=PQ=20\text{ cm}$, $BC=QR=25\text{ cm}$ and $AC=PR=10\text{ cm}$. The three matching sides are equal, so $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle PQR$ (SSS).

spec.description: Horizontal pair, with the second triangle pointing down. Angle values remain inside their respective vertices.
spec.mathematics: BC=QP=3 m; angle B=angle P=70 degrees; angle C=angle Q=40 degrees.

answer.worked: $\angle B=\angle P=70^\circ$, $\angle C=\angle Q=40^\circ$ and the matching sides $BC=PQ=3\text{ m}$. Therefore $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle RPQ$ (AAS).

spec.description: Horizontal pair of obtuse triangles with vertex I, not the numeral 1, on the first triangle.
spec.mathematics: Angle P=100 degrees; angle I=20 degrees; RI=12 cm. Angle C=60 degrees; angle T=100 degrees; UC=12 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Missing angles and congruence result are not shown.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle R&=180^\circ-100^\circ-20^\circ\\\angle R&=60^\circ\\\angle U&=180^\circ-60^\circ-100^\circ\\\angle U&=20^\circ\end{align*}$$
Thus $\angle P=\angle T=100^\circ$, $\angle I=\angle U=20^\circ$ and $RI=CU=12\text{ cm}$. Therefore $\triangle RPI\equiv\triangle CTU$ (AAS).

spec.description: Horizontal pair of downward triangles. Side tick counts are three, two and four, preserving every marked correspondence.
spec.mathematics: TS=GF (three ticks), TP=GM (two ticks), SP=FM (four ticks).
spec.answerVisibility: Side marks only; no answer supplied.

answer.worked: The markings give $TS=GF$, $SP=FM$ and $TP=GM$. All three matching sides are equal, so $\triangle TSP\equiv\triangle GFM$ (SSS).

spec.description: Horizontal pair retaining the two 10 m labels on nonmatching sides and all four supplied angles.
spec.mathematics: EG=YR=10 m; angle G=angle Y=70 degrees; angle M=angle R=50 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: No missing angle or result shown.

answer.worked: The remaining angles are $\angle E=\angle T=60^\circ$. Matching vertices are $E\leftrightarrow T$, $G\leftrightarrow Y$ and $M\leftrightarrow R$. The sides marked $10\text{ m}$ do not match: $EG$ is opposite $50^\circ$, whereas $YR$ is opposite $60^\circ$. Congruence would make $TY=YR=10\text{ m}$, requiring $\angle R=\angle T$, but $50^\circ\ne60^\circ$. Therefore the triangles are not congruent.

spec.description: Horizontal pair preserving double ticks on QF and AH, and all supplied angle labels.
spec.mathematics: QF=AH; angle Q=80 degrees; angle F=30 degrees; angle P=70 degrees; angle H=80 degrees.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle O&=180^\circ-80^\circ-30^\circ\\\angle O&=70^\circ\\\angle A&=180^\circ-70^\circ-80^\circ\\\angle A&=30^\circ\end{align*}$$
Thus $\angle O=\angle P=70^\circ$, $\angle F=\angle A=30^\circ$ and the marked matching sides $FQ=AH$. Therefore $\triangle OFQ\equiv\triangle PAH$ (AAS).
